headline: No major decisions; approved June 15 minutes and discussed consultant David Taylor's research, Henry Austin Barn repairs, and the Lockkeeper's House lease.
summary: Approved the minutes of the June 15 meeting. No other votes were recorded. Discussion covered consultant research, Henry Austin Barn repairs, and the Lockkeeper's House lease, which is expiring without direction from the Mayor's Office.

decision_evidence.quote: Todd Levine moved to approve the June 15th meeting minutes, seconded by Paul Geary. June 15th minutes were approved.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Historic Properties Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
7:00 PM, September 21, 2026 
  
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER   
 Commissioner and Chair Todd Levine called the meeting to order at 7:03 PM. 
2. ATTENDANCE   
 B&C Clerk Porsche Edmundson took attendance: 
Present: Chair, Todd Levine, Paul Geary, Mark Osenko, and Mike Miller from the 
community. 
  
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 Todd Levine moved to approve the June 15th meeting minutes, seconded by Paul Geary. 
June 15th minutes were approved.  
4. PUBLIC COMMENT   
 Mike Miller attended as a member of the Public. He was promoted to panelist status, but 
he did not accept or speak. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE   
  An email from Mike Millicent, representing the Farmington Canal to the Rail Association, 
was identified and forwarded to the commissioner. 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 
 
7. REPORTS   
 
 
  1. Local Register Properties.  
  Discussion centered on consultant David Taylor, who was instructed in May to 
provide more substantive research. He sent no communication throughout the 
summer. Attempts to contact him yielded no updates. If the Commission 
doesn't receive a response by the October meeting, it may consider termination 
of the contract. 
 Financial notes: 
 Approximately $7K–$8K spent
Plan to reapply for additional funding of $20K 
 Total expected rebid budget: $32–$33K 
 Existing research is superficial and largely cut-and-paste. 
  2. Historical Society.  
  No updates at this time. 
  3. Hamden Cemeteries.  
  No updates. Commissioners noted past cleanup events and questioned 
whether they occurred this year. 
8. OLD BUSINESS   
 
 
  1. Mile Markers.  
  The DOT was contacted several months ago, but no response was received. 
Follow-up planned. 
  2. Henry Austin Barn.  
  Multiple attempts were made to contact the Mayor’s Office. 
Town staff member (Stephen White) reported: 
• Brookvale Barn is moving toward posting for work. 
•  The barn requires additional funding or alternative sources. 
• Town Hall and Keefe Community Center exterior work is next. 
• No immediate plan for Henry Austin Barn repairs. 
 
Past slate roof quotes: 
•   $22k patching  
•  $200k full replacement. Because the property is not on the National 
Register, federal funding can't be accessed.  
  
  3. Lockkeeper's House.  
  Owned by DECG; leased long-term to the Town for Police substation use. 
 The lease is expiring; the Mayor’s Office has not provided direction. 
The garage is deteriorating and considered hazardous. Exterior paint is peeling; 
the interior is stable. 
 
  
9. NEW BUSINESS   
 There was no new business to present at this time. 
10. ADJOURNMENT   
 Chair, Todd Levine, moved to adjourn the meeting at 7:30 PM, seconded by Paul Geary. 
Minutes Taken, by B&C Clerk Porsche Edmundson
